newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran, EU miss chance for fresh start.
newsitem.headline: Iran, EU miss chance for fresh start.

text.p: Iran and the European Union appear to have missed an opportunity to make a fresh start in thorny relations by failing to agree on procedures for the return of EU ambassadors to Tehran, diplomats said on Sunday.
"The idea was that (Mohammad) Khatami's inauguration on Sunday (as Iran's new president) offered a very good opportunity to solve the problem," a Western diplomat said.

Khatami, elected by a landslide in May, was confirmed as president on Sunday by supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in a ceremony to which all ambassadors accredited by Iran -- but not their deputies -- were invited.
The ambassadors, including EU envoys, were also invited to Khatami's oath-taking in parliament on Monday.

"Nothing is impossible," said one diplomat close to efforts to resolve the dispute over the manner of the diplomats' return. "But it is far too late now and I think the EU has given up" on using the Khatami inauguration to send back their envoys.
The EU ambassadors left Tehran after a German court concluded in April that Iran's top leaders ordered the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.
At the same time the EU suspended ministerial contacts with Iran and halted its policy, championed by Germany, of "critical dialogue" with the Islamic republic.

Iran, furious at the implication of its top leadership, recalled its ambassadors from European capitals in retaliation and insisted German ambassador Horst Beschmann should be the last EU envoy to return.
The EU refused to allow Tehran to dictate its terms.
Iran said on Saturday night the ambassadors were welcomed to return and "admit they made a mistake", insisting the German should be the last man in.
The EU proposed working around the demand by making other EU ambassadors fly back to Tehran with the German envoy who would be the last man to disembark from the aircraft.
Diplomats said Iran rejected that proposal but appeared to ease its demand.
"When the idea was first floated, Iran said the German ambassador could return 10 days after the others but later dropped it to one day" as the inauguration date got closer, one diplomat said.
But the EU refuses to fall in with Iran's plan.
"The EU will not send back the ambassadors if the German ambassador is the last one in," said the diplomat. "It is self protection because it could happen to any of us in the future."
The EU negotiations with Iran were conducted by Luxembourg which is current holder of the rotating EU presidency but does not have an embassy in Tehran.

Diplomats said the Iranian Foreign Ministry would have liked to deal with each EU state bilateraly. "The leverage as a single group is much greater. We could not have them single out one country like this."
But even if the two sides eventually reach a formula it would not be the end of Tehran's troubles with the EU.

While some EU states see Khatami as a moderate Iranian clergyman they realise he would be commiting political suicide if he attempted early in his presidency to resolve the lingering dispute over a death edict by late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini against British author Salman Rushdie for blaspheming Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".
